rows.heading: Principles of Financial Delegation
rows.quote_snippet: 1.1 Constitutional Authority: Under Section 179 of the Companies Act, 2013, the Board of Directors of ONGC delegates financial and administrative powers to specified executive levels to facilitate agile and decentralised operational decision-making. 1.2 Fundamental Delegation Principles:    (a) Powers are delegated to posts, not individuals. Powers shall be exercised only by the substantive holder of a post or an officer formally designated as in-charge by an office order.    (b) Exercise of powers is subject to approved budgetary provisions (BE/RE), technical sanction, and established procurement procedures.    (c) No authority may sanction expenditure for their own personal benefit or override higher authority reservations.    (d) Five-tier governance structure: Level 1 (CMD), Level 2 (Functional Directors), Level 3 (Key Executives / Asset Managers / EC), Level 4 (GMs/CGMs), and Level 5 (Sectional In-charges).

rows.heading: Commercial Confidentiality of Operational Schedules
rows.quote_snippet: 8.1 Commercial Sensitivity: The detailed schedules of delegated powers, proprietary procurement limits, field-specific financial delegations, and vendor sanction thresholds constitute commercially sensitive internal information. 8.2 Internal Controlled Classification: This Book of Delegated Powers is classified as an Internal Controlled Document. Unauthorized publication, sharing with external contractors, or public disclosure is prohibited under corporate confidentiality regulations.
